calls.reason: Only NVIDIA's own financing blog and Ramp adoption data are offered; neither separates demand Huang created from demand from real workloads.

DOJ charges against other people, Culper's short-seller allegations and the NYT report on the probe's transfer do not show NVIDIA itself knowingly took part; DOJ notes NVIDIA put Megaspeed on a no-sell list.

Huang did resign (8-K), but Reuters on Nov 16 reported financing partners still discussing deals, no sign of a pause, and existing commitments expected to stand, which is against the claim that dependents are out of luck.
Broadcom's $16.7B in quarterly AI chip revenue and Alphabet's meaningful TPU system sales show large competing demand with no shown NVIDIA dependence, which undercuts 'entirely'.
Consumer evidence is mixed (HBS: 2.9% paying; survey: 63% willing to pay) and nothing measures whether paying compute customers can afford it.
Morningstar supports AI driving 2024 market gains, but reporting that Midjourney was profitable in 2023 contradicts the claim that only chipmakers made money on AI, though that report is secondhand.
